fields.h1: Build a Shift Change Form That Confirms Coverage First
fields.hero_description: Build a shift change form that gets the covering coworker's yes, counts overtime and sends each request to the right manager.
fields.features_heading: What a Shift Change Needs Before Approval
fields.features_subheading: Six parts Emergent builds into the form, so a manager decides with the cover and the hours already known.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the request type

Pick swap and the form asks who is covering and which of their shifts you take in return. Pick drop and it asks only for the shift and the reason, with no trade questions.
fields.feature_2:
A yes from the coworker taking the shift

The covering coworker gets a link by email or Slack to accept or decline. Managers see a request only after that coworker accepts, so no approval rests on a guess about cover.
fields.feature_3:
Weekly hours added up before approval

The app adds the new shift to the hours each person already has scheduled that week. Any change that crosses the limit you set is marked in red and held for a manager.
fields.feature_4:
Each location's requests to its own manager

Requests from the downtown store go to its manager in Slack and the airport store's go to another by email. A request left undecided for 24 hours sends that manager a reminder.
fields.feature_5:
One row per change in a database you own

Every request saves who asked, who covered, who decided, and when. An approved change updates the schedule table and can sync to the scheduling tool you connect through its API.
fields.feature_6:
The full codebase, yours to move

On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository and host the form on servers next to your HR systems. Keep building on it in your own editor or with more prompts.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Employers Handle Shift Changes
fields.tab_content_1:
Hamish sees it only after Esteban agrees

Zofia Kral wants Saturday night off and offers her telemetry shift at Harlow Bay Medical Center to Esteban Molle. He accepts on his phone first. Only then does it go to Hamish, the charge nurse, with both nurses marked as telemetry trained. He approves, and the unit schedule shows Esteban on Saturday night.
fields.tab_content_2:
Picked up 14 minutes after it was posted

Nobody volunteers for the 6 a.m. Sunday opening at Brisk Bean. Tadeo can't make this one and drops it into the open pool. Every barista trained to open gets a Slack message, and Oksana claims the shift 14 minutes later. The store manager approves her pickup in Slack.
fields.tab_content_3:
Soraya decides any swap with overtime in it

Bartek has 40 hours at Bramblegate Distribution this week when he asks for a coworker's 6-hour Friday shift, which would make 46. Federal law gives covered employees overtime pay for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. That swap waits for Soraya, the shift lead, to decide.
fields.tab_content_4:
No one at Quayside changes more than Remy

Quayside Grocers keeps every shift change, approved or declined, in one table. Store manager Delvin sorts October's changes by employee. Remy leads with 6 changes against a store average of 2, every one a Saturday morning. Delvin takes Remy off Saturday mornings rather than approve the same swap each week.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Shift Change Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a shift change form that confirms who covers each shift and puts the manager's decision on record.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the changes you allow
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Get the coworker's answer on record
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether staff can swap with a coworker, drop a shift into a pool, or move to another shift on the same day. Each becomes a request type with its own questions. Anything outside those types is a conversation with the manager, not a form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For a swap, the first question is the coworker taking the shift and which of their shifts comes back in return, if any. A request with no named cover is a drop, and it goes to the open pool instead.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Send the covering coworker the request by email or Slack with accept and decline buttons. Save the time they answer. A manager approving a swap later should see that the other person agreed, not take it on trust.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Total the week for the person taking the shift, with the new hours included. Set the line where a request needs a second look, such as 40 hours, and mark those requests so the overtime is visible before anyone decides.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Check the cover can work that station
fields.howto_step_5_des: List the roles each employee is trained for, such as opening the store or working a telemetry unit. Offer each shift only to people on that list. The coworker picker then never shows someone who cannot take it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Pick the approver for each location
fields.howto_step_6_des: Route each request to the manager of the store, unit, or warehouse where the shift happens. Set a reminder for any request with no decision after 24 hours, and name a backup approver for the days that manager is off.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a swap as an employee, accept it as the coworker, and approve it as the manager. Check that the schedule table changed and that the request row shows all three people with times. Fix any wording with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a shift change form?
faq_plan.a: A shift change form is the request an hourly employee submits to swap, drop, or move a scheduled shift. It records the shift, the coworker covering it, and the reason. A manager then approves or declines it before the schedule changes.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a shift change form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder: the request types you allow, who has to accept, and who approves at each location. Emergent builds the form, the approval steps, and the database behind them. Change any part of it later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a shift change form and a schedule change form?
faq_plan.a: A shift change form moves one shift, such as Saturday night, to another person or time. A schedule change form changes someone's regular hours from a set date, such as evenings only starting in September. Keep them as separate request types, because a lasting change needs a different approver.

faq_plan.q: Should new hires be able to use a shift swap form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once their training shifts are done. Block swaps out of any shift marked as training, since that shift pairs the new hire with a trainer. When the training period ends and the new hire turns in a training feedback form, open the shift swap form to them like anyone else.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a schedule change form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the employee, the current schedule, the requested schedule, the start date, and the reason. Add whether the change is permanent or lasts a set number of weeks, and who picks up the hours being given up. Skip the cover question when the new schedule gives up no hours.

faq_plan.q: Should a shift change form ask employees for a reason?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as one short line. A reason helps a manager weigh a dropped shift that has no named cover, while a swap between two trained coworkers can go through without one. Leave medical and family details off the form, since the field is there to help the manager decide.

faq_plan.q: How does a shift change form know who is qualified to cover?
faq_plan.a: It checks a list you keep of who is trained for each role. Record each sign-off with an employee training form and keep both forms in one database. The coworker picker then shows only people signed off for that station, and a new sign-off adds that person the same day.

faq_plan.q: How much notice should a shift change form require?
faq_plan.a: Pick a cutoff that matches how fast you can find cover, such as 48 hours before the shift. Requests made inside that cutoff skip the open pool and go straight to the manager on duty, with an alert in Slack or by email. Emergent builds that rule from one sentence in your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a shift change form update the schedule after approval?
faq_plan.a: Yes. When a manager approves, the app writes the new name onto the shift in the schedule table it keeps. If you run scheduling in another tool with an API, the app can sync the change there too. Emergent builds the request history into a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a shift change form pass on to the coworker taking the shift?
faq_plan.a: It should pass on the handover the regular worker would get: open tasks, notes from the last shift, and any equipment checks due. In a warehouse, that means the incoming operator fills out a forklift inspection form before driving the truck that shift.

plan.angle: The top 10 is two public-employer PDFs (Boone County, DBHIDS), static template galleries (123FormBuilder, Jotform x2, pdfFiller, pdfRun, Workforce.com) and an Indeed letter guide. Every one is a blank form someone prints or fills in; none shows the employer what happens after the request: the coworker agreeing to cover, the check that the cover can work that shift, the overtime math and the manager's decision. This page is for the employer who schedules hourly staff: four shift change setups built from a prompt (a two-sided nurse swap, an open shift picked up from a pool, a swap that would cross 40 hours, a monthly change history), a how-to on what to ask and who approves, and an FAQ for the person who runs the schedule. It stays clear of recurring availability and time off, which have their own pages.
